# Slider

A slider input component.

<template v-if="language === 'js'">

## slider {#slider-method}

`slider(options)`

Creates a [Slider](#slider-class) client, connects it to the active coordinator and returns its containing HTML element. The vgplot wrapper uses an explicitly supplied API context coordinator when present; the mosaic-inputs helper uses the default coordinator.

</template>

<template v-else-if="language === 'python'">

## slider

`vg.slider(label: str, bind: Any, min: Any = None, max: Any = None, step: Any = None, value: Any = None, **opts: Any)`

Create a slider view with required Python label and binding arguments.

Python input helpers return serializable View objects, rather than DOM widgets or MosaicClient instances. The bind argument serializes as as, source serializes as from, and other keyword names use camel case. Options whose value is None are omitted before aliases are applied; for example menu(bind=selection, as_=None) retains the bind argument. False, zero and empty strings remain present. Unknown keyword options are retained for custom clients.

Python slider requires label and bind arguments. The declarative schema requires only the input discriminator, and native JavaScript accepts an optional options object. Consequently a minimal declarative slider can be valid while its emitted Python call requires additional authoring arguments. With a Selection, point clauses compare for equality and interval clauses span the minimum through the current value. With a scalar Param, the value is assigned directly.

</template>

## Declarative options

The JSON/YAML object uses `input: "slider"`. Only this discriminator is required. Native JavaScript uses the options object without the discriminator.

| Option | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `as` | No | The output selection. A selection clause is added for the currently selected slider option. |
| `field` | No | The database column name to use within generated selection clause predicates. Defaults to the `column` property. |
| `select` | No | The type of selection clause predicate to generate if the **as** option is a Selection. If `'point'` (the default), the selection predicate is an equality check for the slider value. If `'interval'`, the predicate checks an interval from the minimum to the current slider value. |
| `from` | No | The name of a database table to use as a data source for this widget. Used in conjunction with the `column` property. The minimum and maximum values of the column determine the slider range. |
| `column` | No | The name of a database column whose values determine the slider range. Used in conjunction with the `from` property. The minimum and maximum values of the column determine the slider range. |
| `filterBy` | No | A selection to filter the database table indicated by the `from` property. |
| `min` | No | The minimum slider value. |
| `max` | No | The maximum slider value. |
| `step` | No | The slider step, the amount to increment between consecutive values. |
| `label` | No | A text label for this input. |
| `value` | No | The initial slider value. |
| `width` | No | The width of the slider in screen pixels. |

## Slider {#slider-class}

`new Slider(options)`

Native JavaScript class extending [MosaicClient](../core/client). Its `element` property contains the input DOM. The constructor accepts the same native options as the helper. Python does not export this JavaScript runtime class.

The Menu, Search and Slider runtime clients retain database query activation, DOM event handling and Param/Selection updates. Native JavaScript options can include element and, for Menu, format; these host values are outside the JSON/YAML input schema.

A filter selection recomputes inferred minimum, maximum and step values; explicitly supplied bounds and steps remain fixed. Empty filtered results retain the previous range.

Native JavaScript clients accept an existing container DOM element; declarative input definitions do not serialize DOM nodes.

## Executable starters

The shared starters create a three-row SQL table, bind a named Param or Selection, and return live inputs. The filtered slider starter links a category menu to the slider range. JSON/YAML declare the view, JavaScript returns DOM, and Python serializes a Spec.

| `slider-filtered` | [JSON](/templates/inputs/basic/slider-filtered.json), [YAML](/templates/inputs/basic/slider-filtered.yaml), [JavaScript](/templates/inputs/basic/slider-filtered.js), <a :href="withBase('/templates/inputs/basic/slider-filtered.py')" download>Python</a> |
